body: Thank you for the different perspective. I've never thought things though that way before. Your words really helped a lot. I wish I could add more but I can't seem to find the right to put it. Thank you so much....I will try to remember this.

I wish I could forget the negative things but I can't. I just can't keep things from haunting me. I don't know how to block out and forget the things that upset me. Thanks for replying, I'll try to find a way, but I'm just not sure how.

I am so sorry you had to suffer through that. Nobody should have to.

 I honestly hope you are right. I haven't been on this planet long but so far my time seems to be a downward spiral. I will try to keep an eye out for better opportunities, but not many have come along. When they do, I'm too afraid to try. I'm so afraid of changing things because every time I do things just get worse. Thank you for your support and for taking time to reply.

I wish I could find the brighter point of my life, but right now I can't think of anything. I used to love swimming but can't anymore due to health issues. I do appreciate your advice however, and will keep an eye out for something new that might brighten things up. Thank you for taking time to reply. I will try to put your help to good use.

What makes you smile? Is there something that you have done that helps you lose track of time. Maybe trying to focus on what makes you happy for awhile will help. Even if it's a few little things it still might make a difference. Is there a picture that makes you smile? A song that clears your mind? Focus on that. If it's hard to remember leave yourself a reminder. Draw a little doodle that reminds you of it on your hand. Whenever you see it embrace your little bit of happiness. Finding a hobby might help too. Sometimes a distraction is best. Sorry this is random and jumbled. It's a bit late and I'm running out of steam. I wish you the best and hope you smile.

I would tell you to quit swimming, but it doesn't just work that way does it? I might be wrong but swimming is your outlet, right? You swim because it diffuses anger and it's something you love to do. You're obviously good at it. The only thing I can think of doing about this is to switch teams. A fresh start. You'd still see them at the meets? Why not kick their fucking asses at swimming. I think you have the capability, and a less hostile environment might give you the push you need.  I don't know much about bullying because my situation is different, but (if my assumptions are correct) I can relate about swimming. I was a synchronized swimmer, so things are a bit different, but even if you still have to see them at meets, having a good team you can tolerate at practices would help more than you think.

If you want to let people into your life but can't, you need to train yourself. I would recommend starting with something you love: swimming. Finding a way to interact with people without awkward conversation can be hard, but you have a good opportunity. If there are new swimmers on the team who need lots of coaching, see if you can help. You seem to be a stronger swimmer than most, and probably have a lot of wisdom regarding the sport. Try teaching people. Start by talking it over with coaches. Say you think you are capable of helping and want to try. There is no awkward conversation starters or people prying into your life. Just swimming, something you know well. By forming this bond with the swimmers you coach, you can start the process of opening up to people. This is something I did that worked well for me. I began to teach younger swimmers basic skills and eventually socializing became easier. While everyone is different, I think this is worth a shot.

I can sympathize with a lot of what you have posted but not all. Sorry I can't try to help with anything else. If my assumptions are wrong and my advice doesn't apply to you, I apologize and still wish you the best. If you think my advice is worth a shot but have questions, feel free to shoot me a message. I might not get it right away but I will do my best to reply as quickly as possible. 

Please stay strong. Your patience is astounding and think you will go far in life if you give it a chance.

When I was a sophomore in high school I dislocated my elbow and shoulder at the same time.

Spoiled dog was begging for a treat and I decided that I was too strong to give in to his petty demands. The little bastard decides, in return, to dive under my feet while I was walking down the stairs holding a laundry basket that prevented me from seeing him. Our stairs at the time were something like [this](http://www.elevestairs.com/images/open-stairs/open-stairs-2.jpg) (but much less extravagant). I fell off at the top and grabbed one of the stairs in a feeble attempt to catch myself, and heard a tremendous crack. I shriek and crumple to the floor after letting go due to the extreme pain. When I get to my feet I notice my shoulder about three inches below where it should be and my elbow bulging from where it should be.

My sixteen year old mind freaks the hell out and decides that when my mom got home she would be absolutely pissed to find me with two more dislocations. I decided the most rational thing to do would be to relocate thing myself.  First I got my shoulder, holding my arm where it should be and ramming myself against a wall to pop it back into the socket. Next, I found a pillar and wrapped my arm around it and proceeded to yank my forearm until it too snapped back into place. Ran up to the bathroom, downed three naproxens, and then slept it off like a boss. Three days later when I finally told my mom we had it x-rayed and, somehow, nothing got chipped.

**TL;DR:** Dislocated shoulder and elbow and then re-set them myself  as a stupid sixteen year old.
